scope: Ghostget 0.18.38 rollout: pin bump in packages/textbutler/src/imessage-setup.ts, a bounded intent-arbitrated send retry in packages/transport/src/automation.ts, and a 60s local fast-driver budget in packages/textbutler/src/fast-driver.ts.

rounds.design: Repin by editing VERSION only; treat run.by-intent as a settle surface; keep the shared 20s fast-driver timeout.
blockers: The wire protocol had to be proven unchanged: the transport speaks ghostget.messaging-automation/1 and the staged 0.18.38 connector still serves that exact string, verified by direct source comparison.

run.by-intent is read-only arbitration, not settlement: a non-terminal (started/indeterminate) row correctly leaves a send unproven, so claiming the pin alone removes the uncertain-send treadmill would be false.

On the live 0.18.38 connector, reply sends repeatedly died in the pre-insert provider chain (poll/status/resolve/insert) while their ack landed: runByIntent returned null — proof the send never started — yet the run terminally failed and the owner saw a bare ack with no reply. The ledger makes exactly one retry safe because a late-committing first attempt returns its stored row under the same intent instead of double-sending.

kind:local fast-driver calls cross the habitat bridge and provider runtime with observed 11-19s latency, so the shared 20s ceiling produces systematic timeouts under load while the gateway path still merits the tight bound.

rounds.design: Pin 0.18.38; on a provider-stage submit fault whose intent ledger shows no row, rebind the same intent on the live enrollment revision and submit once more, then re-arbitrate; split the fast-driver timeout by kind.
blockers: The retry must not synthesize a second intent: it reuses the plan's exact intentId and the already-admitted upstream actions, so serve-side intent dedup still binds the outcome.
A fault in the retry's read-only rebinding (history/prepare) is still a proven non-send and returns dispatch-failed; only a second dispatch fault or a non-terminal ledger row reports indeterminate.
Enrollment identity binds the connector implementation, so the pin lands only after the deployed state was re-enrolled against 0.18.38 with contact ids, settings and grants preserved.
acceptedNits: The retry does not scope-check the arbitrated row's planId, matching prior arbitration semantics; enrollment and intent equality are still asserted before recording.
The version gate runs only in the native setup path; a live daemon does not re-pin per spawn, and the deployed connector is swapped by reviewed host configuration.
localTimeoutMs is a plain 60s bound rather than a measured budget; it trades worst-case hang time for eliminating systematic timeouts, and external abort signals still cap it.
Docs retain the admission-pending caveats because artifact admission and live conversation checks are still outstanding for this pin.
rounds.verification: imessage-setup 23/23 including the expanded refused-version list; transport automation 15/15 with a new regression proving a refused-but-unrecorded send rebinds and dispatches exactly once (2 submits, 1 arbiter read, submitted); fast-driver 5/5; admission gate accepts the regenerated receipt. Live 0.18.38 connector verified byte-identical to ghostget e8bdbfe across five key files; seven contacts re-enrolled; daemon healthy on settings revision 46.
